title: Assessment of somatosensory profiles using quantitative sensory testing (QST) in patients with mast cell activation disease (MCAD)
summary:
Mast cells are involved in the body's immune defense. Pathological changes affecting these cells can lead to a condition known as mast cell activation disease (MCAD). While mastocytosis is characterized by an elevated number of mast cells in the body, mast cell activation syndrome (MCAS) is primarily characterized by increased mast cell activity. In both conditions, the excessive release of mast cell mediators can cause recurrent or persistent symptoms affecting not only the skin, gastrointestinal tract, and cardiovascular system, but also the nervous system. Possible neurological symptoms include altered skin sensitivity and pain.

This study aims to investigate skin sensitivity, including pain perception, in patients with mast cell activation disease (MCAD). For this purpose, quantitative sensory testing (QST) will be used to determine sensory thresholds of the skin in response to different stimuli, allowing the derivation of individual somatosensory profiles. These profiles will be compared with those of healthy controls. In addition, the study will investigate whether associations exist between the QST findings and the patients' clinical characteristics. The study aims to contribute to a better understanding of the role of mast cell mediators in skin sensitivity, particularly pain perception.
conditions: Mast cell activation syndrome (MCAS; ICD-10-CM D89.4x)
Histiocytic and mast cell tumours of uncertain and unknown behaviour

interventions.name: Patients with a diagnosis of mast cell activation disease (MCAD): A one-time quantitative sensory testing (QST) assessment will be performed, together with the collection of clinical and lifestyle-related data using a questionnaire. Healthy controls: A one-time quantitative sensory testing (QST) assessment will be performed, together with the collection of clinical and lifestyle-related data using a shortened questionnaire.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Confirmed diagnosis of a mast cell activation disease (MCAD):
- Mastocytosis according to the World Health Organization (WHO) diagnostic criteria
- Mast cell activation syndrome (MCAS) according to the diagnostic criteria proposed by Afrin, Molderings et al. (2020)
• Prior provision of study information and written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
• Inability to provide written informed consent
• Inability to follow the verbal instructions required for quantitative sensory testing (QST)
• Regular use of analgesics, psychotropic medication, or other medications that may affect pain perception within the previous 4 weeks
• Contraindications to quantitative sensory testing (QST): skin and soft tissue disorders, pregnancy, or breastfeeding
